newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to negotiate cuts to "bitter end" - Treu.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to negotiate cuts to "bitter end" - Treu.

text.p: The Italian government is ready to negotiate public spending cuts "to the bitter end" to ensure they are agreed by the end of September, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said in an interview published on Sunday.
"We have prepared the ground for the final stretch for which, providing there is willingness to do so, we will only need a few days," Treu told daily Corriere della Sera newspaper.
"But if it's necessary, we'll negotiate to the bitter end because we have to decide (spending reforms) by the end of September," he said.
He declined to say whether the government would press ahead on spending cuts without agreement from trade unions.
"I don't want to consider this because up to now we have worked well together. But everyone knows that the objectives (of the government's three-year economic plan) have to be fulfilled."

The government is engaged in negotiations with unions and business leaders aimed at securing agreement on a reduction in spending on state pensions, in order to help Italy qualify for the first round of Europe's planned monetary union in 1999.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi will close the first round on Tuesday before the government takes its summer break.
The government aims to get the reforms finished to coincide with the presentation to parliament of the 1998 budget, which must be introduced by September 30.
Treu said harmonisation of pension regulations, which would signify cancellation of the so-called "baby pensions" in public employment, would be one of the first tasks addressed in September.
Under Italy's pensions' system some workers, dubbed baby pensioners, can retire after paying just 35 years of contributions.
Treu said much progress had already been made in working out public spending reforms in some areas, including in the employment sector.
